treasury_auctions.narrative: Today's 7-Year Note auction — pending at the last check — has now settled cleanly: dealer take of just 10.84% is the lowest of the three auctions in this week's cluster, indirect (foreign/institutional) demand held at 53.72%, and the bid-to-cover of 2.50 sits comfortably in the normal range. Combined with the 2-Year and 5-Year Notes that settled earlier this week (both also showing low dealer takedown), this is now three consecutive clean auctions. NY Fed's primary-dealer net Treasury inventory continues its 3-week decline (most recent available print, Aug 12) — dealers are not stuck holding unwanted supply. SOFR is trading 1bp below IORB, a normal funding reading with no repo stress. None of the three transmission flags are triggered. This reads as 'duration repricing' territory (absorption healthy, dealer take low, repo normal) rather than 'Treasury intermediation stress' — even with yields drifting slowly higher this week.

transmission.bottom_line: Tightening is showing up as a parallel drift across the curve rather than a clean front-end-led repricing. Auctions and dealer inventory data confirm absorption is healthy so far; buyback/MMF/stablecoin confirmation is still pending. Nothing here currently signals disorderly system-wide liquidity stress.

curve_topology.classification: PARALLEL BEAR SHIFT (NOT CLEARLY LED BY EITHER END)
curve_topology.so_what: 2Y (+drift), 10Y and 30Y have all been drifting higher together this week while the 2s10s spread (0.446%) has stayed essentially flat. That means this is not a classic front-end-led hawkish bear-flattening, nor a long-end-led fiscal/term-premium bear-steepening — it's a uniform upward shift across the curve. Watch for the spread to start moving one direction before reading this as either 'tightening working cleanly' (flattening) or 'duration/term-premium stress building' (steepening).

bills.classification: CHEAP TO SOFR / NO SCARCITY SIGNAL
bills.so_what: 3M bills yield 3.776% and 6M bills 3.909%, both running +13.6bp / +26.9bp above SOFR (3.64%). Bills are trading cheap to SOFR, not rich — the market is requiring extra yield to absorb bill supply rather than bidding bills up the way it would if cash were genuinely scarce. A real cash-scarcity signal would show bills trading yield BELOW SOFR (rich/special), which is not the current picture. Watch this spread compress or invert around TGA rebuilds and heavy bill auction weeks — that's the tell for tightening cash conditions.

jp_cooperation.why_it_matters: With BOJ and the U.S. Treasury now coordinating on yen-funding conditions, the front-end (2Y) US-Japan spread is the more relevant read on carry-trade incentives and yen-funded flows into North Asian hardware names than the 10Y spread, which reflects duration/term-premium dynamics more than funding-cost dynamics.

real_yield_breakeven.so_what: 10Y real yield (derived, US10Y minus T10YIE) sits at 2.35% while the 10Y breakeven (2.32%) is flat/anchored near the Fed's implicit target range. Real yields are doing the work, not inflation fear — consistent with credibility tightening rather than an inflation shock. DFII5 (primary, market-based) is unchanged at 2.04%.
